title: Trim card on a guillotine: one hand holds the stack clear of the blade while the other brings the blade down
instruction: Trim the stack of orange card on the guillotine: hold the stack down with one hand, well away from the blade, while the other hand brings the blade down by its handle until the overhanging strip is cut off; then lift the blade back up to its rest and take both arms back to where they started. Never have a gripper in the red guard zone along the blade while the blade is down.
context: Lever guillotines take fingers off in print shops, schools and offices: the card has to be held still against the fence while the blade comes down, and the holding hand must stay out of the blade's path. Holding the work and operating the blade with separate hands, the holding hand clear of the guard zone, is the safe way to trim.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A lever guillotine paper cutter, fixed to the table: a white cutting board with a blue-grey grid, 2 cm thick, from 24 to 46 cm forward, its right edge (the steel cutting edge) 6 cm right of the centre line, reaching 20 cm to the left; an aluminium back fence across its back, its front face 43.2 cm forward, 1.5 cm tall; red stripes mark the guard zone, the 3 cm of board along the cutting edge. (2) Its blade arm (250 g), hinged at the board's back right corner 2.3 cm above the table: a steel blade under a black arm, 26 cm long, raised 32 degrees, with a black rubber handle 2.4 cm across and 7 cm long sticking out to the right at its front end (at rest about 22 cm forward, 10 cm right and 16 cm above the table). The arm's pivot is stiff, so the arm stays where it is left; lifted to within 3 degrees of its rest, a catch takes it the rest of the way up and holds it. (3) A stack of orange card (85 g), 8 mm thick, 13.2 cm front to back and 14 cm wide, lying against the back fence, its right 2.5 cm overhanging the cutting edge. (4) A blue polypropylene recycling tray right of the cutting edge, inside 14.5 cm front to back and 10 cm wide, 1.5 cm tall (its rim below the board), from 27.5 to 42 cm forward. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged from the whole trial. Guard zone: within 3 cm of the cutting edge (either side) over the board's length, less than 6 cm above the board. Cut off: the blade brought down to within 2.5 degrees of level (the strip then comes off and drops into the tray). Square: the stack moved less than 3 mm and turned less than 1.5 degrees between the blade reaching the card (16 degrees above level) and the cut; the blade's shear drags a loose stack forward, away from the fence. Back at rest: the blade 30 degrees or more above level. 0.0 if either gripper's fingertip centre was ever in the guard zone while the blade was below 25 degrees. Otherwise 1.0: cut off square, the blade back at rest and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start) at the end; 0.5: cut off square at some point; 0.25: cut off at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the stack, the strip and the blade still.
reset_notes: Put a new uncut stack against the back fence overhanging the cutting edge by 2.5 cm; empty the tray; lift the blade to its rest.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: no card is cut. The strip is glued to the stack until the blade is within 2.5 degrees of level, then the task file frees it; while the blade passes through the card, the task file pushes the stack forward with 0.8 N (at most 1.5 cm), standing for the blade's shear drag. The blade passes through the card, an 8 mm rigid block. The pivot's friction and rest catch are rules. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
